title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Management Team
tiers.description: The Directors, CEO, CFO, and any other persons having authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling the Company's activities. May not Trade at any time, including during a Trading Window, without the Chairman's prior written approval.

tiers.name: Restricted Person (not Management Team)
tiers.description: Employees nominated by the Board under 6.1 (corporate/divisional accounting officers, confidential secretaries/assistants, employees with access to financial results) who are not on the Management Team. May Trade during a Trading Window without individual prior approval, subject to no Inside Information and no short-term/speculative purpose.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Subset of the Management Team; distinguished for the margin loan approval requirement (3.4) and for notifying the Secretary of Trades to enable Appendix 3Y lodgement (5.7).

tiers.name: Chairman
tiers.description: Distinguished only for clearance: the Chairman's own Trades are approved by a Director chosen by the Board (Chosen Director) or the CEO if none is chosen.

tiers.name: related parties
tiers.description: Family members, nominee companies and family trusts of a Restricted Person, and any investment manager acting for the Restricted Person or a related party. A Restricted Person who is prohibited from Trading must use best endeavours to prohibit Trading by these persons.

windows.start_anchor: close of trading the day after the Company is admitted to the official list of the ASX
close of trading the day after the Company announces its half-yearly results to the ASX
close of trading the day after the Company announces its full year results to the ASX
close of trading the day after the Company's annual general meeting (assuming an update of the full year's results is given)

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may decide any other period during which Restricted Persons are prohibited from trading (Prohibited Period, para (b) of that definition), and may also determine additional periods to be part of the Trading Window (para (e) of that definition). The policy does not state whether either determination is announced or confidential.

rules.detail: Securities expressly include 'hedging mechanisms or derivative instruments'. A non-Management Restricted Person may Trade in these during a Trading Window without individual prior approval if they have no Inside Information and it is not for short-term/speculative gain, but must notify the Secretary of the completed transaction within 14 days. No approval route exists for such a person to Trade outside the Trading Window, as Authorised Trade approval under 5.3 is only available to the Management Team.
rules.evidence: Securities include securities of any kind including ordinary shares, preference shares, debentures, convertible notes, options and hedging mechanisms or derivative instruments.

rules.detail: A Management Team member may not Trade in Securities (including derivative/hedging instruments) at any time, even during a Trading Window, without the Chairman's prior written approval (or the Chosen Director's/CEO's, for the Chairman's own Trades); approval is only granted for Trading Window Trades or defined exceptional circumstances, and lasts until the end of the window or 7 days, respectively.
rules.evidence: A member of the Management Team may not Trade at any time, including during a Trading Window, unless they obtain prior written approval from: (a) the Chairman, in the case of the Management Team

rules.detail: Same regime as derivatives: hedging mechanisms are expressly Securities; permitted during a Trading Window without individual approval, subject to no Inside Information and no short-term/speculative purpose, with 14-day post-trade notification.
rules.evidence: Securities include securities of any kind including ordinary shares, preference shares, debentures, convertible notes, options and hedging mechanisms or derivative instruments.

rules.detail: A hedging mechanism is a Security; a Management Team member needs the Chairman's prior written approval to Trade it at any time.
rules.evidence: A member of the Management Team may not Trade at any time, including during a Trading Window, unless they obtain prior written approval from: (a) the Chairman, in the case of the Management Team

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. As an agreement to dispose of Securities, or a right/obligation to dispose, it is a Trade; permitted during a Trading Window without individual approval, with 14-day post-trade notification.
rules.evidence: Trade means to apply for, acquire or dispose of Securities or to enter into an agreement to apply for, acquire or dispose of Securities or to grant, accept, acquire, dispose, exercise or discharge an option or other right or obligation to acquire or dispose of Securities

rules.detail: A monetisation structure is a Trade; a Management Team member needs the Chairman's prior written approval at any time.
rules.evidence: Trade means to apply for, acquire or dispose of Securities or to enter into an agreement to apply for, acquire or dispose of Securities or to grant, accept, acquire, dispose, exercise or discharge an option or other right or obligation to acquire or dispose of Securities

rules.detail: Short selling as a technique is not mentioned anywhere in the policy.
Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere in the policy.
CFDs are not named but fall within 'hedging mechanisms or derivative instruments'; a Management Team member needs the Chairman's prior written approval to Trade one at any time.
rules.evidence: Securities include securities of any kind including ordinary shares, preference shares, debentures, convertible notes, options and hedging mechanisms or derivative instruments.

rules.detail: A Director may enter into a margin loan or similar arrangement over Securities with the Board's prior approval; if material, the Company may need to publicly disclose the key terms.
rules.evidence: Directors must obtain the Board's approval before entering into a margin loan or similar arrangements concerning Securities.

rules.detail: Clause 3.4 is expressed to apply only to Directors; the policy is silent on margin loans by non-director Management Team members or other Restricted Persons.
'Margin loan or similar arrangements concerning Securities' extends to granting security generally; requires Board approval.
rules.evidence: Directors must obtain the Board's approval before entering into a margin loan or similar arrangements concerning Securities.

rules.detail: 'Margin loan or similar funding arrangements' concerning Securities is broad enough to cover a bank loan secured on the collared shares, requiring Board approval; if for a material number of Securities, the Company may need to publicly disclose the key terms including trigger points and the lender's unilateral sale right.
rules.evidence: Where a Director has entered into margin loan or similar funding arrangements for a material number of Securities, the Company may need to disclose the key terms of the arrangements, including the number of Securities involved, the trigger points, the right of the lender to sell unilaterally and any other material details.

rules.detail: Trading for short term or speculative gain is prohibited for all Restricted Persons; no defined holding period.
rules.evidence: for short term or speculative gain

clearance.evidence: To obtain approval, members of the Management Team must send an email to the Chairman ... setting out the details of the potential Trade ... If granted, the approval will last: (c) for an approval to deal in shares during a Trading Window, until the end of the Trading Window; or (d) for an approval to deal in shares due to exceptional circumstances, for 7 days from the day the approval was granted.

clearance.approver: A Director chosen by the Board (Chosen Director) or the CEO if there is no Chosen Director
clearance.evidence: in the case of the Chairman, a Director chosen by the Board for that purpose (Chosen Director) or the CEO if there is no Chosen Director.
Each Trader must notify the Secretary of the details of completed transactions within 14 days after each transaction. Notification is necessary whether or not prior authority was required.
Directors must obtain the Board's approval before entering into a margin loan or similar arrangements concerning Securities.

short_term.evidence: for short term or speculative gain

exceptions.evidence: transfers of Securities already held by a Restricted Person into a superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which the Restricted Person is a beneficiary

where a Restricted Person is a trustee, Trading by that trustee provided the Restricted Person is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decision to Trade during a Prohibited Period is taken by the other trustees or by the investment managers independently
undertakings to accept, or the acceptance of, a takeover offer

Trading under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the Security Holders, such as a pro-rata rights issue, a security purchase plan, a dividend or distribution reinvestment plan and an equal access buy-back, where the plan that determines the timing and structure of the offer has been approved by the Board
disposals by a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under an approved margin lending arrangement

the exercise (but not the sale of Securities following exercise) of an option or a right under an employee incentive scheme, or the conversion of a convertible security, where the final date for the exercise of the option or right, or the conversion of the security, falls during a Prohibited Period

Trading under a non-discretionary trading plan for which prior written approval has been provided in accordance with this Policy provided the Restricted Person did not enter into the plan or amend the plan during a Prohibited Period
to sell Securities to realise cash in a time of exceptional financial hardship (excluding a tax liability)
to comply with the requirements of a Court order or enforceable undertaking

financing_disclosure: Directors: when a margin loan/similar funding arrangement covers a material number of Securities - to the Company/market - trigger is materiality under the Listing Rules as the Company determines, no fixed deadline stated - disclosure to include number of Securities, trigger points, the lender's unilateral sale right and other material details.

exemption_authority: The Chairman (or the Chosen Director/CEO for the Chairman's own Trades) may grant written approval for a Management Team member to Trade in exceptional circumstances - financial hardship (excluding tax liability), a court order/enforceable undertaking, or where delay would cause greater hardship, family detriment, or breach a court order - provided the Trade is lawful, not for short-term/speculative gain, does not exploit Inside Information, and would not appear unfair; the approval must state its period and lasts 7 days.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Securities include securities of any kind including ordinary shares, preference shares, debentures, convertible notes, options and hedging mechanisms or derivative instruments.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An OTC put and call sold by a bank are expressly 'Securities' under this definition, so the collar's derivative legs are directly and expressly regulated by the Policy, not merely inferred.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors must obtain the Board's approval before entering into a margin loan or similar arrangements concerning Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A director may enter the collar's loan leg (secured on the collared shares) with prior Board approval - there is no outright prohibition, unlike some peer policies, but the process is Board-level, not a single officer's sign-off.

bespoke_clauses.clause: for more than $50,000 worth of Securities to any party if written approval from the Chairman is not obtained, covering the form of and timing of the sale, and the management of its public disclosure, before entering into discussions for the potential sale of those Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any collar-sized position (almost certainly over $50,000) triggers a separate Chairman approval covering timing, form and public disclosure management, before even entering into sale discussions - relevant to structuring the written call and any unwind.

bespoke_clauses.topic: Management Team can never trade freely
bespoke_clauses.clause: A member of the Management Team may not Trade at any time, including during a Trading Window, unless they obtain prior written approval from ... the Chairman
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A likely collar counterparty (director, CEO or CFO) needs the Chairman's prior written approval for every trade, including inside a Trading Window, so entry, adjustment and unwind of both collar legs each require individual sign-off.

bespoke_clauses.topic: public disclosure of margin loan terms
bespoke_clauses.clause: Where a Director has entered into margin loan or similar funding arrangements for a material number of Securities, the Company may need to disclose the key terms of the arrangements, including the number of Securities involved, the trigger points, the right of the lender to sell unilaterally and any other material details.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If the collar's financing leg is material, the Company may be required to publicly disclose its size, trigger points and the bank's unilateral sale rights.

bespoke_clauses.clause: disposals by a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under an approved margin lending arrangement
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement sale on default is an Excluded Trade, so it is not blocked by a Prohibited Period and needs no fresh Chairman/Board approval - a clean lender remedy, provided the original margin loan was itself approved.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The policy makes no reference anywhere to 'unvested', 'vesting' or a 'holding lock'.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike several peer policies, MGH does not separately restrict hedging, derivatives or margin loans over unvested equity incentives; the general Trade/Trading Window/Management Team approval regime is the only gate, aside from the Excluded Trading carve-out (f) that blocks selling securities obtained on exercise until the relevant exercise date has passed.

summary: A funded collar is achievable for a Director under this policy, but with layered approvals. The derivative legs are expressly 'Securities' (hedging mechanisms or derivative instruments); a non-Management Restricted Person could trade them during a Trading Window with only post-trade notification, but a Management Team member (the likely counterparty) needs the Chairman's prior written approval for every trade, in or out of a Trading Window. The loan leg is a margin loan or similar funding arrangement concerning Securities, permitted for Directors with the Board's prior approval, and if material the Company may need to publicly disclose its size, trigger points and the bank's unilateral sale right. Any trade over $50,000 additionally needs Chairman approval covering timing, form and disclosure before discussions even begin, which will almost always apply to a collar-sized position. A lender's forced sale on default is an Excluded Trade requiring no fresh approval. Overall: workable with Board approval for the financing leg and Chairman approval for each derivative leg and any large unwind, and there is no vesting-state carve-out to navigate.
